findings: The ruling is Primer Tribunal Ambiental case R-21-2019, dated and signed in Antofagasta on 27 Oct 2020 (p. 1, p. 54; the file name says 26 Oct). It decides a claim filed 22 Mar 2019 by the Comunidad Indígena Aymara de Quillagua and the Comunidad Indígena Quechua de Huatacondo against SMA Res. Ex. N°24 of 26 Feb 2019, which approved SQM S.A.'s third (refundido) compliance program in sanction procedure Rol D-027-2016 and suspended that procedure (p. 1). D-027-2016 concerns SQM S.A.'s Pampa Hermosa project (RCA N°890/2010), eight charges about the hydraulic barrier and monitoring of the Salar de Llamara puquios (pp. 16-17). The court rejected the claim in all parts and kept Res. Ex. N°24 in force, without costs (p. 54). It neither annulled an approval nor ordered anything, and it does not concern the Salar de Atacama or SQM Salar's F-041-2016 program; 'Atacama' and 'F-041' do not occur in it. It cites an earlier ruling of the same court, R-17-2019, on another point (p. 34) without saying what that case concerned. So the entry's link of the 2022 program to R-21-2019 (via Minería Chilena) is not supported by the ruling; either the article or the entry's transcription names the wrong case. Record and gap amended; no rows changed.
new_record: Chile's Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente (SMA) opened sanction proceeding Rol F-041-2016 in November 2016 after an audit found brine over-extraction and incomplete information (six infractions [press: Diario Financiero, Minería Chilena]; charge 1 covers brine extraction above the authorised amount between August 2013 and August 2015). The SMA approved SQM Salar's compliance program by Res. Ex. N° 38/2022 of 29 August 2022 (cost more than CLP 46,000 million [press: Diario Financiero], about USD 52 million [press: Reuters via Mining.com]). The program steps the average maximum brine extraction down to 822 L/s from 2027 (slightly under 50% of the limit in RCA 226/2006), a step tied to an EIA still under evaluation, with a limit of 1,026 L/s for the 2025–2026 environmental year, and caps industrial freshwater pumping at 120 L/s (-50% versus RCA 226/2006). SQM filed progress report 15 of 20 on 27 Feb 2026 (program period 30 Aug 2022–28 May 2027). Minería Chilena links the program to the Primer Tribunal Ambiental's ruling in case R-21-2019 [press: Minería Chilena], but that ruling (27 Oct 2020) concerns another procedure: it rejected a claim by the Aymara community of Quillagua and the Quechua community of Huatacondo against SMA Res. Ex. N°24 of 26 Feb 2019, which approved SQM S.A.'s compliance program for the Pampa Hermosa project (Rol D-027-2016, Salar de Llamara), and left that approval in force. Reuters describes the 2022 program as a revision of a previous plan 'mandated by a local environmental court in 2020' [press: Reuters via Mining.com]; no ruling on F-041-2016 was read.
new_gap: Regulator record (822 L/s from 2027, conditional on a pending EIA; 1,026 L/s in 2025–2026) and company claim (50% by 2030) point the same way; no measured extraction volumes against these limits found yet in the documents read. The court ruling that preceded the 2022 program in F-041-2016 is not identified in the documents read; case R-21-2019 concerns Pampa Hermosa (D-027-2016).

findings: The G.R. confirms each policy term the entry had from summaries: target of 7.5 GW (§4(b), p. 3; §7.9, p. 10 also limits incentives to an aggregate 7.5 GW); 'a minimum of 51%' of electricity for core operations from green and renewable energy (§7.1, p. 9); 100% reimbursement of electricity duty actually paid for 20 years from commercial operation (§6.1 item 5, p. 6); 'Essential Service' under the Gujarat Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1972 (§8, p. 10). Water: captive desalination support of 20% of capex or INR 2 crore/MLD, whichever is lower, for plants up to 20 MLD per GW, scaled pro rata (§6.3, p. 8); 24x7 water to the doorstep (§6.5, p. 9); entities 'expected' to meet water needs primarily through captive desalination 'wherever feasible' (§7.11, p. 10). Also: INR 1 per unit power-tariff reimbursement for 20 years (§6.1 item 3); eligibility from 150 MW approved IT load (§7.6); incentives capped at 75% of EFCI, disbursed over 20 years, 5% a year (§7.2-7.3); EFCI capped at INR 60,000 crore per GW (§5(d)). The G.R. does not mention Jamnagar, Reliance, Meta, 168 MW, or a Rs 6 lakh crore investment figure. Record rewritten from the G.R.; requirement rows re-sourced; four rows added.
new_record: Gujarat DST G.R. No. DST/MIT/e-file/24/2026/0624/IT (approved 06-08-2026) issues the Viksit Gujarat Data Center Policy (2026-29). Data-centre entities must source a minimum of 51% of electricity for core operations from green and renewable energy (§7.1). Incentives include 100% reimbursement of electricity duty actually paid for 20 years from commercial operation, power-tariff reimbursement of INR 1 per unit for 20 years, and capital support for captive desalination plants up to 20 MLD per GW of data-centre capacity (§6.1, §6.3); the State is to supply 24x7 water to the doorstep, and entities are 'expected' to meet water needs primarily from captive desalination where feasible (§6.5, §7.11). Only projects with approved IT load of 150 MW or above qualify, and total incentives are capped at 75% of Eligible Fixed Capital Investment (§7.2, §7.6). Data-centre operation is an 'Essential Service' under the Gujarat Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1972 (§8). The G.R. does not mention Jamnagar, Reliance, Meta or 168 MW.
new_claim: The policy's target is the establishment of 7.5 GW of data-centre capacity in Gujarat (G.R. §4(b); the Gujarat government's own aim). An investment figure of ~Rs 6 lakh crore is reported by SuperKalam citing The Indian Express and does not appear in the G.R. The same summary reports the Reliance-Meta Jamnagar site at 168 MW initial capacity using renewable energy and desalinated seawater for cooling. Reliance has publicly described the Jamnagar project as the world's largest AI data centre (gigawatt-scale) in press coverage.
new_gap: The G.R. sets incentive terms and conditions but no water-use or electricity-use limits for any site; no High Powered Committee approval, water permit or desalination plant record for the Jamnagar site was located, and the 168 MW initial capacity and the Rs 6 lakh crore figure rest on a tertiary summary of press.
